page: Amazon Web Services m6g.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The system features 8 physical cores powered by AWS Graviton processors with ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Each virtual CPU maps directly to a dedicated physical execution core without simultaneous multithreading (SMT). Cache provisioning comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes hardware cryptographic acceleration via ARM AES instructions, while lacking x86-specific SIMD instruction sets such as AVX or AMX.

Benchmark evaluations position the m6g.2xlarge in the middle tier for multi-threaded computation and standard application execution. In stress-ng testing, it achieves 1,519.4 on single-core and 12,135.21 on multi-core runs. Geekbench results reflect single-core scores of 936.0, situated in the bottom 10%, alongside an average multi-core score of 5,355.0 and clang compilation score of 8,588.0. Uncached read memory bandwidth achieves 120.79 GB/sec with write bandwidth at 55.91 GB/sec. The instance delivers steady performance in I/O and server routines, recording 9.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.38 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, raw scalar compression and decompression lag, as shown by single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.3 GB/sec and weak extended instruction benchmarks.

The m6g.2xlarge does not bundle local NVMe storage, meaning disk input/output operations rely entirely on external network-attached block storage. Additionally, hardware accelerators are absent, with 0 GPUs available. Large language model inference remains limited on this architecture, delivering 35.33 tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter models and 6.71 tokens per second on 7B models. From a resource perspective, the Graviton Neoverse-N1 cores provide predictable per-core CPU execution due to the absence of hyperthreaded resource contention, rendering the profile suitable for microservices, Redis in-memory caches, backend application runtimes, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance based on AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz under the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration includes 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, 32.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The server includes no bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight solid multi-core throughput, recording 12,135.21 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 9.56 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads, and 9.38 GB/sec in static web serving. While single-thread decompression and mathematical vector workloads exhibit weaker metrics, the dedicated core architecture offers consistent execution without hyperthreading overhead. It is appropriately deployed for Redis caching tiers, web application servers, microservice container hosting, and general business logic.

32.0 GB system memory providing a balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio
